transcript.text: Beko vented dryer, drum goes round fine but it's just blowing cold air. Had it about 6 years. What part do I need?

I can't give you a specific part yet because 'blowing cold air' on a vented dryer is most often caused by blocked airflow tripping the safety cut-out, rather than a broken component. If the lint filter or rear vent hose is clogged with fluff (very common after 6 years), the heater will shut off to prevent overheating. Please check if your fluff filter and rear vent hose are clear of blockages. Clean them if needed and run a normal heat programme for 10 minutes. If it still blows cold air, I can then guide you through checking the heating element or thermostat.
Done that. Filter was fairly full and the vent hose had a sag full of fluff, cleaned both out. Ran it 20 min and it's still cold. Can't see a reset button on the back either. What part now?

The most likely cause on a 6-year-old Beko vented dryer is that the heating element has burned out and stopped conducting electricity. Another possibility is that the thermal cut-out (a safety device) has failed or remains tripped, but given the age, the element itself is the primary suspect. To distinguish between these, you need to check if the element still conducts current. Please unplug the machine, access the heating element (usually behind a rear panel), and test it for continuity with a multimeter. If there is no continuity (infinite resistance), the element has failed and needs replacing.
I haven't got a multimeter so can't do the continuity test. Is there any other way to tell which part it is, or should I just order the element?

Without a multimeter there is no reliable way to distinguish between a failed heating element and a blown thermal cut-out, as both result in cold air. Since you cannot test it electrically, the practical solution is to check the heating element assembly (which often includes the thermal cut-out or thermostat). If replacing these parts does not restore heat, the issue may lie with the main control board or wiring, which would require a qualified engineer.
